paper_title: Searches for electron interactions induced by new physics in the EDELWEISS-III germanium bolometers
notes: Paper presents three main results: (1) Solar axion CBRD search: g_ae < 1.1×10^-11 at 90% C.L. in massless limit (Eq. 11, Fig. 3). This is a mass-independent bound valid for m_a well below solar core temperature (~keV). (2) Solar axion 57Fe line search: g_ae × g_aN^eff < 3.5×10^-17 at 90% C.L. (Eq. 12, Fig. 4), shown as function of axion mass. (3) Bosonic dark matter absorption: bounds on g_ae and κ (kinetic mixing) in mass range 0.8–500 keV/c^2 (Fig. 5). Primary AxionElectron coupling type identified from CBRD signal proportional to g_ae^2 and direct electron absorption cross section. DM density ρ_DM ≃ 0.3 GeV/cm^3 used for dark matter absorption calculations (Eq. 3). The CBRD bound (Eq. 11) is mass-independent and encoded as horizontal line. The 57Fe and DM absorption results are mass-dependent and would require digitization of figures for precise extraction; only the primary CBRD limit is extracted as text value. Paper also reports electron decay lifetime τ_e > 1.2×10^24 years but this is not a coupling constraint. The EDELWEISS-III constraint (solid red line) forms the lower boundary of the excluded region (shaded pink area above). The boundary shows a relatively flat profile at ~1.1×10^-11 for low masses (below ~0.1 keV/c²), then gradually decreases as mass increases. The plot also shows constraints from EDELWEISS-II (dashed red), XENON100, PandaX-II, and LUX experiments, as well as theoretical predictions (DFSZ and KSVZ models shown as shaded regions). The text confirms g_ae < 1.1×10^-11 at 90% C.L. in the massless limit.
